name: Rudimental
notes: ⛔ **This model extends `liquid-dnb`, not `dance-pop`.** The volume writes Rudimental up in the `dance-pop` section, and states in its own assignment notes that the entry keeps the genre-native grammar — "Rudimental's 170-180 two-step" — "rather than forcing them onto a four-on-the-floor". The entry names the lane directly: "**liquid drum and bass** grammar — a fast syncopated breakbeat at 170-180 with the two-step kick/snare skeleton". Extending that lane is what the encoding contract asks when the research marks the case explicitly. The band is that quoted spine and nothing wider — floor 170, ceiling 180, the entry's own "a **170-180 DnB spine**" with "the breakthrough single reads 180 at full rate, 90 halved". The entry's separate "**86-125 house/pop side** for the later crossovers", where "it is a straight 2&4", is the other rhythmic family and is not modelled here; the single that "reads 159" is left out for the same reason. The deltas against `liquid-dnb` are the ones the entry documents. The backbeat moves: "kick on 1, snare on the 3rd beat of the bar — which *feels* half-time against the 175 grid", so `halfTime` is true and the snare sits on `halftime_3` where the parent has a straight 2&4. The feel is played, not programmed — "live percussion and a real drummer's feel are layered in", with credited instrumentalists — so `quantizeStrength` falls to 0.78 with a 0.24 velocity variance, the loosest grid in anything this agent wrote. The liquid convention "explicitly uses fewer bar-oriented samples", so the perc bed is a ghosted 16th ride and shaker rather than chopped breaks. The low end is the parameter the entry says makes these read as songs rather than club tools: "sine sub-bass and 808-style low end doubled by played bass guitar, moving in half-note or whole-note pedal tones under the fast drums — the low end is slow while the drums are fast", which is a kick mirror at 0.92 roots with a low anticipation. Harmony is "soul/gospel — ii-V motion, 7ths and 9ths, and a modulating or plagal lift into the chorus — because the toplines are written for gospel-trained singers", and the palette is live brass: "the chorus bursts open with soul-flying brass". Guest vocalists rotate, which is why the entry sits in PRODUCERS. ⚠ The exact drum placement is DnB/liquid convention by the entry's own statement; the velocities, densities and registers are INFERRED. ⛔ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than `reese_sustain`, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm `bass.rs` reads that holds a note, and it emits one note per chord — TASK-162, still open — so this model measured **261 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** on it against `bass.rs`'s floor of 500. `mirror_kick` with a high root lock is the roster-wide substitution for a sustained sub (`dmx`, `coolio`, `krs-one`, `mobb-deep` all record the same one), and over a kick that plays the two-step 1 with a `4&` at 175 it reads as held at this tempo. The research is *"sine sub-bass and 808-style low end doubled by played bass guitar, moving in **half-note or whole-note pedal tones under the fast drums**"* — and at 170–180 BPM a bass on this kick *is* a half-note pedal, which is why the substitution costs less here than anywhere else in this batch. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.92 and `anticipationProb` 0.14 are lane-conventional; the entry marks its exact drum placement as DnB/liquid convention already.
